instruction: Use a script for mechanical work (counts, diffs, greps, git facts, rule-decided verdicts). Spawn an agent only for judgement.
outcome: On 2026-09-15, 106 agents found nothing and one script found the blocker.
owner_words: mechanical work is a script, agents only for judgement

instruction: Never wait on a job in the foreground. The step that LAUNCHES a job returns INCOMPLETE with the log path and pid, and a later step collects the result. A scheduler that has to wait does it in one scripted call (jobs_wait), never through an agent that keeps re-checking.
outcome: 43 of 294 swarm agents sleep-polled (2026-10-06). 24 collect agents spawned only to answer PENDING read 24.6M tokens (2026-10-07).
owner_words: never wait or poll in the foreground
enforcement: scripts/pipeline/tool_guard.py WAIT (PreToolUse hook); judged-swarm.js waitJobs via scripts/pipeline/jobs_wait.sh

instruction: Never read a big file whole. Find the lines with grep -n or a code-graph query, then read a bounded range.
outcome: Agents start at a median of 70k tokens of context and re-read all of it every turn.
enforcement: tool_guard.py READ (Read or cat of a file over 1000 lines)

instruction: Give every spawned agent a named agent type with a short tools list. Use a minimal generic 'step' charter when no role charter applies.
outcome: A default agent starts at about 95k tokens of context and a restricted one at about 48k: roughly 381M tokens re-read in one session (2026-10-06).

instruction: Keep agent steps short by capping tool calls ([step-cap 30]). Refuse call 31 except a context-file write, return the remainder as nodesLeft, and continue it in a fresh small step.
outcome: Cost grows with the square of step length. Measured: 934.5M tokens read against about 77k written across three swarms; eight developer agents (about 160 calls each at about 324k context per call) were 44% of it. Replaying with a 30-call cap reads about 40% less.

instruction: Read files in windows of at most 200 lines (sed -n A,Bp), after grep -n has located the lines.
outcome: 96 reads over 8 KB in the same swarms (tool_guard.py:27).

instruction: Cite baseline numbers from the baseline script; never re-measure them per agent.
outcome: Removes duplicate measurement runs.

instruction: (Reverted) Poll background jobs with periodic agent WAIT steps. Replaced: wait with a one-call scheduler script instead.
outcome: Agent WAIT/collect steps were assumed to 'cost almost nothing', but 24 collects spawned only to answer PENDING read 24.6M tokens. Replaced by jobs_wait.sh.

instruction: Keep each step's required rule-reading small (operating cards) so it fits the step budget.

Never open a large file to answer 'what calls X', 'who writes Y' or 'what breaks if I change Z'. Ask the graph or a callers query, then open only the named file:line in a bounded window. A file read compounds: it is re-read on every remaining turn.
outcome: Opening a 9,282-line file with 200 turns left costs 22.2M tokens, against 26.6k for graph_query.py callers. A 15-card wave re-read 235,682 tokens per turn over 3,512 turns: the bill is context size times turns, not agent count.

instruction: Before spawning an agent, ask whether a command could answer the question. Counts, diffs, greps, conflicts, git facts, board state and rule-decided verdicts are scripts. Correctness review, acceptance-criterion observables, failure classes and root-causing are agent work.
outcome: Triaging 53 stranded branches: 106 triage and judge agents were killed with no verdicts. One shell script plus one Python file took ~4 minutes at near-zero tokens and found the single systemic blocker.

instruction: Prefer a script even when an agent would work. A script is re-runnable, diffable, committable and idempotent, and it sees the whole distribution, where per-item agents each see one item.

outcome: Budgets came from the 2026-09-04 judge synthesis and were already met by each role's lean rows.

instruction: Delegate measurement (suite, analyzer, gates, battery) to one bounded measurer subagent that returns figures only.
outcome: Measurer budget: 60 turns or fewer, 80 KB of tool results.

instruction: Turn device legs into integration tests the train runs, and shrink spawn injection to a short operating card per role.
outcome: Owner directive #33 (4), via REQ-134/135.

instruction: Put a hard cap on agents per outcome run (default 20). Send every spawn through one counter, and when the cap is reached stop and hand control back to the human/PO. Do not keep spawning.
outcome: Brake logs 'BRAKE: N agents spent; stopping for the PO'. Added because runaway swarms burned hundreds of millions of tokens (REQ-323).

instruction: Give every worker step a tool-call cap written into its prompt ([step-cap N], 30 for developer/fix/audit/prove steps, 15 for judges, 25 for a whole-requirement judge). Before reaching the cap, the step appends at most 6 lines of progress to the ctx file's ## Log and returns what is left, so a fresh step can continue.
outcome: Every call re-reads the whole context, so an agent's cost grows with the square of its length. Eight developer agents averaged ~160 calls at ~324k tokens of context per call, 44% of three swarms' reads. Replaying the transcripts with a 30-call cap read ~40% less (a replay estimate, not a live after-measurement).
owner_words: Token usage must be absolutely optimal
enforcement: scripts/pipeline/tool_guard.py:23,53,154-173 LENGTH refuses call N+1 for a subagent whose prompt carries [step-cap N]

instruction: Never open a whole large file. Find lines with grep -n, then read windows of at most 200 lines.
outcome: Cuts per-call context size, which compounds across every later call.
enforcement: prompt text; tool_guard READ/RANGE per CLAUDE.md

instruction: Never paste big outputs, and cite file:line for every claim.
outcome: Part of the token discipline appended to every swarm prompt.

instruction: Run a mechanical check as a dedicated step agent with a single exact command. Use exactly one tool call, return only rc and the last line, never run anything else, and use the cheapest model/effort.
outcome: Mechanical work costs two model turns instead of an agent's reading (see jobs_wait measurement).
enforcement: workflow prompts with agentType 'step', model 'haiku', effort 'low'

instruction: Charge rulings against the agent budget (one-way = 3 agents, two-way = 1) and cap rulings per run (2 in an outcome run, 4 by default in a backlog run).
outcome: Stops ruling loops from bypassing the agent cap.

instruction: Cap steps per lane (default 25) and agents per backlog run (default 200), with a brake that stops spawning when the cap is hit.
outcome: Runaway prevention.

instruction: Give each build wave an agent budget (default 15 + 25 per lane). A wave that spends its budget without a judge PASS gets no further agents, and the run stops and hands back to the PO.
outcome: Earned by REQ-323 wave 1, which spent ~130 agents with no judge PASS and nothing stopped it.
owner_words: my tokens are wasted a lot

instruction: Orient from the shared ctx file without reading it whole. Grep the marker of the previous stage (cut to 300 chars) for binding rulings, tail the last 6 lines for the latest log, and never print a whole section. Obey those rulings, and append at most 10 lines under ## Log when finished.
outcome: Earned by D90: ctx files grew, and whole-file reads were costly.

instruction: Continue a capped step in fresh continuation steps (up to 8). Each continuation is told which nodes earlier steps finished, never to redo them, and to do ONLY the remainder.
outcome: Small windows instead of one long context.

instruction: Developer and fix steps never start or wait on long jobs (mutation battery, full suite, gates). They run only the affected tests in the foreground. Long jobs belong to the verifier, launched and waited on by the scheduler.
outcome: Earned by REQ-323 (2026-10-07): fix continuations launched batteries, then spent eight steps re-checking them, each counting as 'progress' for one checked job.

instruction: Wait for background jobs with one call of a wait script in a lean step (cheapest model, low effort, at most 110 s per call, about an hour in total). Spawn a collect only after the jobs have ended.
outcome: Measured 2026-10-07: 24 collects in the REQ-306 and REQ-323 journals were spawned only to answer PENDING, reading 24.6M tokens, and every chain ended UNVERIFIED.

instruction: REVERTED rule: do not spawn a test agent to find out whether a background job has ended.
outcome: Failed at 24.6M tokens over 24 PENDING-only collects, with every chain UNVERIFIED (six back-to-back collects against a battery queued an hour for a suite slot). Replaced by the one-call waiter script.

instruction: Cap launch steps like any other step. Return probes, rows or jobs not yet started as the remainder, and list every started job so it reaches the collect.
outcome: Launches had run 50-83 uncapped calls, using 69M of REQ-306's 163M tokens.

instruction: Use the cheapest model and lowest effort for mechanical steps (waiting, ticking, checker runs) and medium effort for template-driven generation (plan/tasks).
outcome: Lower token cost for work that needs no judgement.

instruction: Keep the always-loaded instruction file to an operating card of at most 200 lines. It holds every rule that decides an action and names every refusing script. Move the long form verbatim with pointers. A policy check enforces the cap. Ship with before/after token measurement and revert if the cut is under 30%.
outcome: CLAUDE.md was 1,469 lines (~25-30k tokens), injected into every spawn. The queue reported 15 runs / ~4.5M tokens, 654k on one run. The trim was mandated with a revert condition.
enforcement: scripts/policy_check.sh (card over 200 lines refused); agent_efficiency.py before/after

instruction: Cap the shared per-requirement context file (12 KB) and re-fold it before dispatching the next stage, because every agent reads it first.
outcome: The ctx was 18,813 B when ordered re-folded to 12 KB or less.

instruction: Orient each role with a targeted grep of the context file for the previous stage's rulings plus its last few lines. Never read the whole rulings section.
outcome: Measured 58,830 bytes (whole section) against 1,430 bytes (stage grep): 41x less on every spawn. A later edit back to 'sed -n the whole Judge rulings section' (33,616 bytes) was reverted (D92(5)).

instruction: A PreToolUse guard hook must fail open on its own errors, never cap the main session, and leave the structured return tool outside its matcher. Prove it does not falsely cap uncapped agents by checking where injected text lands relative to its scan window.
outcome: Measured: hook 57 ms on a 2.1 MB transcript. In 410 of 433 transcripts the injected CLAUDE.md starts at byte 104,725 or later, outside the 64 KB window, so there were no false caps. Reproduced test_tool_guard 36/36.

instruction: Cite evidence already held for the same tree (same blob/md5). Never re-run it. After an edit, re-run only the rows whose code the edit touched.
outcome: The verifier cited run 9773 as the GREEN half and re-ran only seven rows. battery-rest3 stays valid for rows outside the edited function.

instruction: Never wait on a job in the foreground: no sleep loops, no sleep of 5 s or more, no polling; run long jobs in the background and let a separate step collect.
outcome: 43 agents found sleeping on their own jobs; the step that launches a job must never see its result (directive #48).

instruction: Never read a file over 1000 lines whole (Read without limit or whole-file cat); grep -n first, then a bounded read.
outcome: A file read is re-read on every later turn; a 9,282-line service file alone motivated BIG=1000.

instruction: Read line windows of at most 200 lines per sed -n A,Bp call.
outcome: 96 reads over 8 KB found in the audited swarms; the guard refused this session's 221-line window.

instruction: Cap every implementation/fix subagent's tool calls with a step cap (e.g. [step-cap 30]); past the cap the agent may only write progress to its ctx file and return, and a fresh step continues.
outcome: Cost grows with the square of agent length: eight developer agents averaged ~160 calls at ~324k tokens of context per call, 44% of three swarms' reads.
enforcement: tool_guard.py LENGTH rule; judged-swarm stepped() continuation

instruction: Keep always-loaded context (CLAUDE.md and each agent definition) under a byte budget (~32 KB each): one line per rule; move history, incidents and measurements to non-auto-loaded docs.
outcome: 74% of 338M tokens read in one swarm was fixed starting context; a developer agent started at 81k tokens, 40k of it CLAUDE.md (80 KB) and its charter (78 KB).
owner_words: my tokens are wasted a lot

instruction: Inject a short per-role operating card instead of the full charter; each charter ends with a BINDING rules section of ids, and a card missing any id, or a charter with no such section, fails the check.
outcome: Injected context was a quarter of a typical agent's budget before it read code; the id check stops 'shorter' quietly becoming 'weaker' (L-8: a check with nothing to check reports success forever).

instruction: Before launching an evidence job or judge for a task node, refuse if a ruling closed the node or the clean HEAD tree already has a GREEN line for it: cite, never re-run.
outcome: Prevents re-verifying the same tree sha (directive #47 'cite, never re-run').

instruction: Parse agent transcripts mechanically into per-agent command ledgers (turns, tool calls, repeated commands and reads, full-suite runs) so a judge reviews in ~2k tokens.
outcome: Avoids re-reading 300k-token transcripts (directive #28).

instruction: Write workflow args into a relaunch script file (args embedded at the anchor) instead of pasting large args into each call.
outcome: Swarm args ran 8-15 KB and were pasted by hand four times in one day; resumes on another machine need the file.

instruction: Build artifacts once per input tree: content-address them by the tree hash of their inputs and reuse.
outcome: 216 abandoned builds (12 GB) covered 9 distinct trees: 24x duplication, ~9 hours of build for 22 minutes of work, nearly filling the disk.

instruction: Apply doc patches with a deterministic anchored applier: each anchor resolves to exactly one occurrence, all hunks resolve in memory before writing, and every removed line is printed.
outcome: Four rounds spent 117k-291k tokens each on an agent whose only job was transcribing already-written hunks.

instruction: Judge tokens: measure the agents being judged from their transcripts and turn each waste finding (whole large reads, repeated runs on an unchanged tree, re-derived facts, pasted outputs) into a directive.
outcome: Judge check 6.
